Universe is the closed canonical 41-entry set of UNESCO World Heritage Sites with Category=Mixed designation per UNESCO DataHub whc001 dataset. Universe predicate is UNESCO's authoritative `category='Mixed'` flag, equivalently expressible as the set intersection of designated-cultural sites (category IN {'Cultural','Mixed'}) ∩ designated-natural sites (category IN {'Natural','Mixed'}) = 41 IDs (Tongariro id_no=421 is the one edge case included by Category=Mixed designation but excluded by the narrower `criteria_txt contains both cultural and natural codes` predicate — Tongariro has criteria_txt='(vii)(viii)' which are both natural-only codes yet UNESCO classifies it as Mixed from its 1993 associative-cultural-landscape extension). UNESCO is the authoritative source for World Heritage inscriptions; no curator judgment for universe membership. All 5 cell values source-extractive per cycle-1 audit's verbatim 41-row dump. decision_log.decision: Cycle-2 BLOCKING fix: Chiribiquete Site cell — straight ASCII quotes → UNESCO-native curly quotes (U+201C/U+201D)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 post-staging audit's BLOCKING #1. UNESCO DataHub whc001 id_no=1174 `name_en` carries 'Chiribiquete National Park – “The Maloca of the Jaguar”' with curly quotes; cycle-0 staging used ASCII straight quotes drifting from source. decision_log.decision: Cycle-2 BLOCKING fix: Uluṟu Site cell — explicit normalization-policy clarification (NOT a value change)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 post-staging audit's BLOCKING #1 second clause. UNESCO DataHub raw `name_en` for id_no=447 carries 'Ulu<U>r</U>u-Kata Tju<U>t</U>a National Park' with embedded `<U>...</U>` underline markup. Staged Site cell uses rendered Unicode underdot diacritic form 'Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park' (matches UNESCO public Web view + Wikipedia + standard Aboriginal orthography). Policy choice: KEEP the normalized rendered form (NOT change to raw markup) because (a) the rendered form is what UNESCO presents to readers in the public Web view, (b) it matches Wikipedia + scholarly orthography, (c) raw `<U>` markup is internal whc001 storage representation NOT user-facing canonical form. Cycle-2 fix: explicitly document this as a rendering normalization in `normalization_decisions::Site` rule + draft.json `temporal_note::Site-cells` paragraph (was previously implicit/undeclared). NO value change to CSV cell.

decision_log.decision: Cycle-2 HYGIENE fix: db_analog rewrite to reproduce 41-row universe (Tongariro edge)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 post-staging audit's NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. Original db_analog modeled intersection via `cultural_criteria IS NOT NULL ∩ natural_criteria IS NOT NULL` which returns 40 rows (excludes Tongariro National Park id_no=421 because Tongariro has cultural_criteria=null despite Category=Mixed designation — likely from 1993 associative-cultural-landscape inscription extension). Rewritten db_analog uses `category IN ('Cultural','Mixed') INTERSECT category IN ('Natural','Mixed')` then final filter `category = 'Mixed'` which preserves the set-operation INTERSECT semantic AND returns the staged 41 rows. The INTERSECT operation is honest: a row is in both designated-cultural sites AND designated-natural sites if and only if its category is Mixed (since Mixed sites are designated for both cultural AND natural value). Added explicit Tongariro edge note to normalization_decisions::Criteria + draft.json temporal_note.

normalization_decisions.rule: Site designation rendered from UNESCO DataHub whc001 `name_en` field. 40 of 41 cells are raw `name_en` verbatim. ONE explicit orthographic normalization applied per cycle-2 post-staging audit's normalization-policy clarification: UNESCO DataHub's raw `name_en` for id_no=447 contains embedded `<U>r</U>` and `<U>t</U>` underline markup ('Ulu<U>r</U>u-Kata Tju<U>t</U>a National Park'); the staged Site cell renders these as Unicode underdot diacritic characters ('Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park') which is the standard rendered form matching UNESCO's public Web view + Wikipedia + standard Aboriginal orthography. This is the only Site cell where the staged form differs from raw `name_en`; all other 40 cells are verbatim. Verbatim preservation includes: full descriptive titles ('The Ahwar of Southern Iraq: Refuge of Biodiversity and the Relict Landscape of the Mesopotamian Cities'); diacritic verbatim ('Papahānaumokuākea' Hawaiian okina/macrons; 'Pyrénées - Mont Perdu' French acute; 'Göreme' Turkish umlaut; 'Tehuacán-Cuicatlán' Spanish acute; 'Río Abiseo' Spanish acute; 'Türkiye' post-2022 official rename); UNESCO-native curly-quote preservation in 'Chiribiquete National Park – “The Maloca of the Jaguar”' (curly U+201C/U+201D per UNESCO whc001 — corrected at cycle-2 from initial ASCII straight quotes per cycle-2 BLOCKING fix); en-dash separators in 'Mount Kumgang – Diamond Mountain from the Sea' / 'Te Henua Enata – The Marquesas Islands' / 'Paraty and Ilha Grande – Culture and Biodiversity'.

Sovereign country name verbatim per UNESCO official designation. Full official forms: 'United Republic of Tanzania' (NOT 'Tanzania'); 'Democratic People's Republic of Korea' (NOT 'North Korea'); 'Türkiye' (NOT 'Turkey' — post-2022 official rename); 'Viet Nam' (with space per UNESCO; NOT 'Vietnam'); 'United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland' (full UK official name); 'United States of America' (full US official name). Transboundary multi-country sites use comma-delim: 'Lesotho, South Africa' (Maloti-Drakensberg); 'North Macedonia, Albania' (Ohrid); 'Spain, France' (Pyrénées-Mont Perdu).

Closed 5-value categorical per UNESCO official regional classification: 'Africa' / 'Arab States' / 'Asia and the Pacific' / 'Europe and North America' / 'Latin America and the Caribbean'. NOTE: 'Asia and the Pacific' (with 'and the'), NOT 'Asia & Pacific' or 'Asia-Pacific'. 'Latin America and the Caribbean' (with both 'and the'), NOT 'Latin America & Caribbean'.

Integer year of first inscription per UNESCO date_inscribed field. Secondary extension years documented in audit_trail but NOT staged in this column (e.g., Maloti-Drakensberg extended 2013; Lake Ohrid extended 1980 + 2019; Uluṟu extended 1994; Tasmanian Wilderness extended 1989; Kakadu extended 1987 + 1992; Tongariro extended 1993).

Text parenthesized Roman-numeral codes verbatim per UNESCO criteria_txt field. Format: '(i)(iii)(vii)(ix)' for Machu Picchu = cultural criteria (i)(iii) + natural criteria (vii)(ix). 40 of 41 rows have at least one cultural (i-vi) AND at least one natural (vii-x) criterion code in criteria_txt. EDGE PER CYCLE-2 AUDIT: Tongariro National Park (id_no=421, row 16 of CSV) has criteria_txt='(vii)(viii)' — both natural-only Roman-numeral codes — yet UNESCO classifies it as Category=Mixed (likely from the 1993 associative-cultural-landscape extension where the cultural-criteria-list field is null but the Category=Mixed flag is authoritative). Thus the operational universe predicate is `Category=Mixed`, NOT `criteria_txt contains both cultural and natural codes` (the latter would exclude Tongariro yielding 40 rows). The set-operation INTERSECT semantic is preserved by the equivalent membership rule used in db_analog: `category IN ('Cultural','Mixed') INTERSECT category IN ('Natural','Mixed')` = 41 IDs. Range: '(iii)(viii)' Willandra Lakes (shortest 2-criteria Mixed) to '(i)(ii)(iii)(iv)(v)(vii)' Mount Taishan (6 criteria spanning broadest cultural+natural mix).

open_questions.question: When UNESCO inscribes new Mixed sites at future World Heritage Committee meetings, should the instance be re-staged?
open_questions.answer: Yes. UNESCO inscribes ~1 Mixed site per year on average. Mount Kumgang (DPRK 2025) is the most recent staged inscription. Future inscriptions extend universe; instance can be re-staged. temporal_sensitivity = low reflects slow growth.

open_questions.question: Why heritage-properties/world-heritage-sites NEW bucket instead of events/world-heritage-sites?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit required edit. World Heritage Sites are PHYSICAL HERITAGE PROPERTIES (real geographic + cultural units with defined boundaries — Machu Picchu, Mount Athos, Tasmanian Wilderness, etc.), NOT events (point-in-time occurrences like inscriptions or designations). Events bucket would be semantically wrong for the sites themselves; heritage-properties bucket NEW reflects the property-status framing.

open_questions.question: Why use UNESCO DataHub whc001 instead of Wikipedia for source?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit required edit #1. UNESCO DataHub whc001 is the authoritative upstream dataset published by UNESCO World Heritage Centre with category + criteria + year + location fields directly accessible. Wikipedia mirrors may have lag or transcription errors; UNESCO master is canonical.

open_questions.question: Why is 'Türkiye' used instead of 'Turkey'?
open_questions.answer: Per UNESCO official designation: Turkey officially requested its English name change to 'Türkiye' (matching Turkish spelling) at the UN in 2022, ratified by UNESCO + international bodies. UNESCO DataHub whc001 uses 'Türkiye' for Turkish sites (Göreme National Park, Hierapolis-Pamukkale). Source-verbatim preservation.

open_questions.question: What's the database structure of the set_operation framing?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2-rewritten db_analog: cultural_designated_sites CTE = sites with category IN ('Cultural','Mixed'); natural_designated_sites CTE = sites with category IN ('Natural','Mixed'); mixed_sites CTE = cultural_designated_sites INTERSECT natural_designated_sites; final SELECT filters to category='Mixed' and extracts the 5 cell values. This predicate is equivalent to UNESCO's authoritative `category='Mixed'` designation AND honestly reproduces the staged 41-row universe (the cycle-1 original db_analog used `cultural_criteria IS NOT NULL ∩ natural_criteria IS NOT NULL` which returned only 40 rows excluding Tongariro National Park id_no=421 — Tongariro has Category=Mixed with criteria_txt='(vii)(viii)' (both natural-only Roman-numeral codes) and cultural_criteria=null in whc001, likely from the 1993 associative-cultural-landscape extension where the cultural-criteria-list field is null but the Category=Mixed flag is authoritative; the rewritten predicate captures Tongariro because Tongariro's `category='Mixed'` makes it a member of BOTH designated-cultural AND designated-natural sets). The set-operation INTERSECT semantic is preserved: a row is in both designated sets if and only if its category is Mixed (Cultural-only sites are NOT in designated-natural; Natural-only sites are NOT in designated-cultural; only Mixed sites are in both).
